p.write_text('''# 0007. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21

## Context

ADR 0006 made the TypeScript backend a second resolver that finishes components the structural resolver already found. Detection by shape now covers 92 to 99% of the components react-docgen-typescript (RDT) reports on five large libraries (`docs/edge-cases.md`), and what is left is a call with no type argument (`lazy()`, `createIconLoader("x")`) or a prop a callee adds (Mantine's `component` and `renderRoot` on 220 components). Only the checker can answer those: it knows what the call returns. Separately, callisto's rule is no cargo features in shipped crates, which ADR 0006's "feature-gated crate" contradicts.

## Decision

- **Discovery.** The backend may add components the structural pass did not find, using RDT's rule: a declaration whose type has a call signature with a props-shaped first parameter. Each carries the rule that found it and merges into the structural output; on a clash the structural entry wins.
- **Always compiled, enabled at runtime.** `crates/tsc-client` is a normal dependency of the CLI and the NAPI addon, with no cargo feature. A runtime option turns it on and is off by default, so a run without it spawns nothing.
- **Structural stays the default and the fallback.** A missing, unsupported or crashing `tsc` leaves the structural result untouched and adds a diagnostic.
- **Trigger.** The backend runs only for components the structural pass marked incomplete (an opaque leaf, a wrapper call with no resolved props, a callee-added prop it cannot see) plus whole-project discovery when the option asks for it. It is never a silent default.
- **Output.** `ExtractionOutput` gains an additive `schemaVersion` so consumers can tell whether discovery was on. Existing fields keep their shape.

## Consequences

- Wrapper calls the structural pass cannot see become exact without a new heuristic per library.
- Every build pays for the client's dependencies. Users who never enable the backend pay nothing at runtime.
- The checker needs `typescript` 7.1 or later and sees a dependency edit only when told. `WatchSession::update_file` must notify it, with a parity test against `extract()`.
- Checker types do not fit `PropType` losslessly, so a checker answer is converted at the boundary and anything that does not fit stays opaque with a reason.
- Determinism needs a gate: a clean run and an incremental run must agree, measured on the five corpora with dependencies installed.
- Supersedes only the feature-gating bullet of ADR 0006. The rest of 0006 stands.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the backend a feature of a separate crate.** Matches ADR 0006 as written but breaks the no-features rule and makes the shipped binary vary by build.
- **Run it by default.** Costs a process per run on projects that structural detection already handles and makes output depend on a toolchain being installed.
- **Add one structural heuristic per remaining shape.** The remaining shapes need the callee's return type; a heuristic per library is what the shape-based detector was built to avoid.
''')

Phases 0 and 1 are done apart from 0.7, and most of Phases 2 and 3 are done. The recall gaps from the benchmark are mostly closed. It is 19 open PRs in one stack, #52 to #70, plus #46, the 0.2.2 release PR, which is separate. CI is green on #52–#54 and #68; #66 and #69 have Lint, SemVer and MSRV passing with the Test jobs still running; #70 is still running.

**Recall against react-docgen-typescript** (five source-only mirrors, own props):

| Project | Components found, before | Components found, now | Its props reported, now |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mantine | 29% | 93% | 92% |
| Chakra | 9% | 92% | 85% |
| Ant Design | 88% | 97% | 95% |
| shadcn/ui | 98% | 98% | 94% |
| react-spectrum | 98% | 99% | 97% |

- **Biggest fixes:** detecting wrapper calls by shape (`factory<XFactory>(...)`, `withContext<El, Props>(...)`) and following barrel re-exports. Two barrel bugs were behind most of the missing Mantine and Chakra props: `extends` through a barrel, and the `import { X }; export { X }` style.
- **Speed:** Mantine went from 45 ms to 143 ms because it now resolves 346 components instead of about 105. The other four got slightly faster.

**Defects D1–D9** are fixed, except D1 (see Open below). The fixes are:
- parenthesized and `!` wrappers
- same-name enums
- unreadable files
- overloaded diagnostic codes
- `Pick` and `Omit` with generic or `keyof` arguments
- watch mode drifting from `extract()`
- eight options that were accepted and never read

I deleted those eight options rather than wiring them, which is a breaking change under a minor changeset.

**Foundations** (sibling `tests.rs`, strict lints, architecture tests, SemVer and MSRV CI, a cache byte-layout guard, a per-shape recall test) are in. The declared MSRV of 1.94 never built; it is now 1.97. I added ADR 0007 and recorded that `typescript@7.1.0-beta` ships a public API (`typescript/sync`, `/async`, `/proto`) and works with the Rust client.

**Open:**
- **Cannot be fixed structurally** (needs the TypeScript checker): calls with no type argument (`lazy()`, `createIconLoader("x")`, 8 components), and props a callee adds (Mantine's `component` and `renderRoot` on 220 components). This is roadmap items 4.3 to 4.5, a large piece of work I did not start.
- **Not done:** structured type arguments (2.1) and the rest of the architecture refactors (2.3, 2.5, 2.7). A text parser stands in for the type-argument problem. Also not done: 3.5, 3.6, performance work, and the release and site tasks (yank the old crate, update the site page, user guides).
- **Left out on purpose:** no proptest or fuzz targets yet (the golden-bytes test covers the cache layout).

**Things to know:**
- **Wrapper detection is on by default.** The roadmap's D1 recommended gating it behind a flag. I measured about 96% precision on Mantine and drop any guess that resolves to no props. Say if you'd rather gate it.
- **SemVer job.** It would have failed every PR with an intended break. It now passes when a pending minor or major changeset covers the break, and fails otherwise. I re-stacked the whole chain once to put that fix at the base, and again after finding three lint issues of my own.
- **Merge order.** Merge #52 first and go upward in order, one at a time. Every PR in the stack sits on its predecessor, and each lists its base.

I haven't merged anything and there are no draft PRs. #46 (the 0.2.2 release) is separate and still yours to merge.

<pasted_content id="d5b8">
# Caliper v1 review

My release assessment: the project has a credible speed advantage and much better structural coverage than it had a week ago, but the current open stack is not yet a v1 quality gate. I would continue the staged releases in the roadmap (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/08bafb04/docs/projects/architecture-roadmap.md), while treating watch correctness, detection precision, and a reproducible RDT comparison as required evidence before calling the output dependable for v1.

I reviewed the 20 PRs merged since October 14, all 20 PRs open on October 21, the final stacked branch, architecture and ADRs, tests, CI, and release workflow. This was a code and CI review; I did not run a new local build or benchmark. The working tree already contains uncommitted changes, which I left untouched. Entire transcript search could not read its saved Keychain login, so the retrospective relies on commits, PRs, and repository documents.

## What the week accomplished

The merged work renamed and published the Caliper packages, changed package metadata and licensing, updated dependencies, separated large inline Rust test modules, added architecture tripwires, and tightened production lints. The open stack then addresses real defects: deterministic enum selection, unreadable files, diagnostic codes, generic Pick/Omit, barrel resolution, watch parity, and several missed component declaration shapes. These are substantive improvements, and CI is green across the dependent stack.

The measured direction is promising. The roadmap’s latest source-only comparison (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/08bafb04/docs/projects/architecture-roadmap.md) reports component recall against RDT of 93% for Mantine, 92% for Chakra, 97% for Ant Design, 98% for shadcn/ui, and 99% for react-spectrum after #69. Those numbers establish progress on recall in that sample. They do not yet establish precision, output equivalence with dependencies installed, or v1 reliability under incremental updates.

## Findings ranked for release

| Priority | Finding and evidence | Consequence and action |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | The new wrapper rule can emit non-components. #62 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/62) accepts a PascalCase binding when a generic call has a plausible first argument, including any string or identifier; it does not inspect the callee’s return type. A local interface or a type ending in Props is enough to select props (wrapper.rs, lines 43–55 and 105–120 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/08bafb04/crates/core/src/extractor/wrapper.rs#L43-L120)). For example, a Button constant returned as a string by makeLabel<ButtonProps>("button") meets these conditions. | This can inflate recall and pollute consumer output. Before enabling this rule as a default v1 behavior, run the roadmap’s per-family, hand-labeled precision gate, add representative non-component calls, and prefer callee evidence where available. |
| P0 | Watch snapshots can combine different revisions. #67 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/67) repairs several parity bugs, but global, reverse dependencies, named types, components, and diagnostics still publish separately. update_file swaps global, then independently updates the other stores (watch.rs, lines 180–212 and 241–301 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/08bafb04/crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs#L180-L301)); snapshot() reads them separately (lines 129–150 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/08bafb04/crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs#L129-L150)). Concurrent updates can also load a global revision other than the one whose named-type index a call just patched. | HMR consumers can observe stale or mixed props and diagnostics. Implement the documented immutable WatchRevision publication model, then test concurrent old-or-new complete snapshots and clean/incremental equivalence. Serializing updates is a reasonable interim containment measure. |
| P1, confirmed by control flow | Initial watch diagnostics disappear from later snapshots. initialize() receives output from cold extraction and seeds component_cache, but never seeds self.diagnostics; snapshot() reads only that map plus enum diagnostics (watch.rs, lines 110–150 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/08bafb04/crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs#L110-L150)). | A cold parse or I/O error is returned once and then absent from watch --out snapshots until an update replaces it. Add an exact initial-output versus snapshot diagnostic test and persist the cold diagnostics. |
| P1, confirmed by control flow | The Vite virtual module retains removed or renamed components. On HMR, the plugin only assigns updatedComponents into currentOutput.components; it has no removal path (index.ts, lines 175–184 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/08bafb04/packages/vite-plugin/src/index.ts#L175-L184)). Rust #67 evicts a changed file’s old cache keys, but the incremental payload does not convey those removals. | A renamed Card can leave Card beside Panel in the virtual module.     for _ in range(100):

    after = json.loads(out.read_text())

    print('after dep edit   ', summary(after))
    print('cold extract     ', summary(cold1))
finally:
    proc.terminate()
    proc.wait(timeout=5)

  ## Determinism, cache and performance audit, caliper-docgen @ 08bafb04
  
  I ran the prebuilt binary only, without cargo. The worktree is untouched. Scripts and outputs are under `/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/review/perf/`. As you asked, I left out the watch-path correctness bugs and the duplicate-diagnostic ratio.
  
  ### Timings (hyperfine, 10 runs; "cold" means the cache dir was deleted before each run)
  
  | corpus | cold ms | warm ms | peak RSS MB | components |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | mantine | 130.3 | 130.3 | 93 | 346 |
  | chakra | 25.9 | 25.2 | 28 | 516 |
  | antd | 37.8 | 39.6 | 37 | 252 |
  | shadcn | 51.3 | 50.5 | 46 | 1887 |
  | spectrum | 118.0 | 118.4 | 72 | 1381 |
  | mantine + real @types/react, TS 6 libs, `--html-attributes full` | 159.2 | 152.1 | 121 | 346 |
  | synthetic, 10k components (`--json`) | 2700 wall (382 internal) | — | 1939 | 10000 |
  
  Two single runs took about 6 s wall clock but only 0.45 s of CPU. Hyperfine never reproduced this, so I'm treating it as host contention.
  
  **Determinism is clean.** For all 5 corpora in curated and full modes, I compared the full JSON (diagnostics order included, `durationMs` and `dtsCacheHits` removed) across 6 conditions: a cold run, two warm runs, a second cache dir, a copy at another path (paths rewritten back), and that copy with files touched in reverse order. Every result was byte-identical. Discovery is sorted, and the enum and const-array bare indexes are sorted. I found no hash-order leak.
  
  **Robustness is clean.** None of these panicked or hung: a 2 MB random `.tsx`, malformed TSX, 5000-deep `Array<>`, a 3000-deep union, a 2000-level extends chain, a 7 MB file with 60k components (0.27 s, 601 MB), symlink loops, and duplicate file symlinks (deduplicated).
  
  ### Findings
  
  **1. The cache serves stale data after a confirmed extractor change. P0, confirmed from code and git history.**
  - `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 9` (`cache.rs:32`) was last set in 987b6142.
  - cddf6102 then changed `SourceData` for byte-identical input: `import {X}; export {X}` now becomes `ReExportNamed` (`extractor/mod.rs`, `promote_reexported_imports`). The version was not bumped.
  - So any `.d.ts` cached by 987b6142 keeps the old `LocalDeclaration` exports under 08bafb04, with no signal.
  - The pattern: invalidation relies on remembering to bump by hand (ADR-0003 says so). The fix is to key the manifest on crate version plus a build or extractor hash.
  
  **2. The schema version isn't stored in the payload. P2, suspected and not reproduced.**
  - `dts-v1.msgpack` and `manifest.json` are two separate atomic renames (`cache.rs:201-209`).
  - A CLI and a Vite plugin at different versions sharing one dir could pair a v9 manifest with an older positional payload. That decodes as wrong data rather than failing.
  - The fix is a versioned header inside one file.
  
  **3. Full HTML mode fails when `node_modules` sits inside the `--src` dir, e.g. `--src .`. P1, confirmed.**
  - `oxc_resolver::resolve_dts` expects a *containing file* and takes its parent (`dts_resolver.rs:106`). `pipeline/mod.rs:329-330` → `react.rs:134,141` passes a directory, so the lookup starts one level too high.
  - Repro: on the mantine copy with real types, the output says "@types/react could not be resolved". With the same tree laid out as `src/` plus a sibling `node_modules`, it resolves (3 cache entries instead of 2).
  - `import.rs:200` has the same off-by-one for files directly in a package root.
  - Related: `./types.js` ESM specifiers are unresolvable because no `extension_alias` is set. It is diagnosed, but common in NodeNext projects.
  
  **4. Output serialization dominates wall time and memory. P1, measured.**
  - 10k synthetic components: 382 ms internal against 2.70 s wall and 1.94 GB with `--json`. Pretty `--out` takes 5.0 s and 2.55 GB; TOON takes 0.98 s and 1.43 GB.
  - Mantine: 92 ms internal against 130–200 ms wall.
  - Causes:
    - `PropType` serializes by building a `serde_json::Value` tree for every prop (`output.rs:436-439`).
    - The whole output is built as one `String` before `println!` (`cli extract.rs:44,52`).
    - Each prop holds two clones of the absolute file path (`chain.rs:361-362`), about 1.4 KB per prop in memory.
  - Fixes: `to_writer` on a `BufWriter`, a direct `Serialize` impl, and `Arc<str>` for paths.
  
  **5. The DTS cache gives almost no benefit, and its stats mislead. P1, measured.**
  - It only ever caches `.d.ts` files inside the src dirs plus at most 3 lib files. The corpora never hit it (0 hits).
  - With real libs it saves 7 ms (−4.5%) while reading or writing a 2.6–2.8 MB file. `get` clones the about-2.5 MB `lib.dom` `SourceData` on every run.
  - `dtsCacheHits` counts only phase-2 hits (`pipeline/mod.rs:288`), not lib hits (`:491`). Warm runs therefore report 0.
  - A truncated payload, random bytes, a bogus msgpack length and a broken manifest all fall back to an empty cache with **no Diagnostic**, which breaks non-negotiable #6. Output stayed correct in every case.
  - Stale `(path, old-hash)` entries are never pruned. Eviction drops 100 arbitrary DashMap entries (`cache.rs:156-160`).
  - 8 concurrent runs on one dir left a valid cache and identical output. The last writer wins, so the others' entries are lost.
  
  **6. Quadratic inheritance merge. P2, measured on synthetic input.**
  - `merge_parent` (`resolver/mod.rs:492`) rebuilds the set of existing prop names for every parent and clones each prop twice (`:496`, `:499`).
  - Each extends branch also clones 3 `FxHashSet`s (`chain.rs:286-289`).
  - Diamond fan-out: 10k edges take 20 ms, 40k take 90 ms, 160k take 580 ms. Full mode's roughly 300 attributes per layer push real code toward this.
  
  **7. Per-reference allocation and no memoization across components. P2, partly measured.**
  - `resolve_named` and the chain `visit_key` build a key from the full absolute path plus joined args, allocated on the heap for every type reference (`named.rs:30-36`, `chain.rs:38`).
  - Shared base types are re-resolved for every component. Mantine resolves one conditional type 13,358 times.
  - Diagnostics make up 9.1 MB of mantine's 23.5 MB JSON.
  - The fix is a per-run memo of `(file, type, args)` → resolved result plus its diagnostics.
  
  **8. Each watch save costs O(project). P1, suspected from code; latency not measured.**
  - `update_file` deep-clones `GlobalSourceData` (`watch.rs:187`) and rebuilds `ReverseDeps` (`:211`).
  - `ResolutionContext::build` rebuilds `ImportResolutionMap`, a new oxc `Resolver` with a cold FS cache, and re-reads tsconfig (`resolver/mod.rs:184-217`).
  - Key disambiguation scans the DashMap once per affected component, which is O(A·C) (`watch.rs:255-285`). An edit to a shared types file makes that about C².
  
  **Priority order:** 1 and 3 are wrong output. 4 and 8 are the biggest speed risks at scale. Add a regression test that pins `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` to a hash of the extractor's output on a fixture corpus.

# Caliper v1 quality review: Codex findings, vetted and extended Commit reviewed: `08bafb04`, the top of the open stack #52–#70. Repros ran against a release binary built from that commit. They live in `/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/review/`: `vet/` holds mine, and `detection/`, `text-types/`, `parity/`, `perf/` and `dx/` hold the sweeps'. Status labels used below: - **Confirmed**: reproduced by running it. - **Control flow**: proven by reading the code, not run. - **Suspected**: plausible, not proven. ## 1. Verdict on the Codex review | Codex finding | Verdict | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | P0 wrapper rule emits non-components | **Confirmed, worse** | `makeLabel("button")`, `z.object<…>()`, `createStore<…>()`, `createContext(ident)` and zustand `create(fn)` are all emitted. Measured precision is about 1/6 on a negative-heavy corpus. | | P0 watch snapshots mix revisions | **Control flow, and dwarfed** | It holds. But single-threaded watch is already wrong deterministically; see family D. | | P1 initial diagnostics lost | **Confirmed** | Cold `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` vanishes from watch output after an unrelated edit. | | P1 Vite keeps removed components | **Control flow, worse** | Also: keys differ from Rust, diagnostics and enums never refresh, the virtual module is never invalidated (the integration test hides this by calling `invalidateAll()`), and `vite build --watch` ships the first extraction forever. | | P1 wrapper candidate vanishes silently | **Confirmed** | `wrapper.rs:89` `continue`. The recorded candidate also suppresses the old `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE`. | | P1 substitution inside quoted text | **Confirmed** | `Pick` with `T = number` picks the `number` prop. | | P1 RDT advantage not proved | **Confirmed, worse** | The recall metric counts only components with own props. That hid 84 real Chakra components dropped by the empty-props guard. | | Arch: semantic model still text | **Confirmed, worse** | Six P0 classes of silent wrong props; see family C. | | Arch: detection provenance partial | Agree | | | Arch: ADR 0006/0007 merge contract | Agree | My ADR 0007 conflates *discovery clash* with *prop completion*. `schemaVersion` must not double as provenance. | | Arch: resolver → pipeline back edge | True, known | It is allowlisted in the architecture test pending item 2.3. Low priority. | | Arch: watch performance ungated | Agree | Each save is O(project), and key disambiguation is O(A·C). | | `std::collections::HashMap` in pipeline | True | One site, `pipeline/mod.rs:379`. Trivial. | | `visible()` omits diagnostics | True | It also tests only edits to the component's own file. | | Integration tests never run | **Confirmed, worse** | The binding crate is excluded from every test recipe as well, so its 16 tests never run. | | Fuzz/property work deferred | True | | | Docs drift | Confirmed, broader | See family I. | | #44 lint failure | **Codex right, me wrong** | oxfmt 0.73 reformats five files in `docs/archive/`. It is not merely stale, as I said earlier. | One sweep claim was refuted: "the 10 platform packages have no versioning path". Release PR #46 bumps all of them. ## 2. Findings by root-cause family Severity scale: - **P0**: wrong output, no diagnostic. - **P1**: user-visible wrong, stale or missing output. - **P2**: maintainability, performance or polish. ### A. Detection admits on weak evidence (P0) None of the inferred rules requires evidence that the thing renders. - **Typed PascalCase helpers become components.** Confirmed. `TypedFunctionExpression` (`component.rs:188`), `FunctionDeclaration` (`visit.rs:294`) and `HocWrapper` (`component.rs:218`) admit any PascalCase function with a typed first parameter. That includes `FormatName = (u: User) => string`, `function FullName(u): string`, generators, `debounce((q: Row)=>…)`, `createSelector`, `z.preprocess` and `memo((a)=>a.id)`. - **An alias through any call deletes the real component.** Confirmed. `export const MemoCard = memo(Card)` or `getDisplayName(Card)` treats `Card` as renamed and drops the exported `Card` (`component.rs:504`, `mod.rs:267`). - **The wrapper rule's shape test is too weak.** It accepts any identifier or call as the first argument, takes any same-file type including synthesized `__anon_N` aliases, and trusts the `*Props` suffix (`wrapper.rs:45-56`, `:118`). - **Non-exported and nested components are emitted.** Confirmed. RDT emits exported components only. - **Discovery excludes match the absolute path.** Confirmed. A project under `my.test.repo/` yields 0 components and 0 diagnostics (`discover.rs:51`). - **Requiredness and children are wrong.** `Required

` is unwrapped as transparent, so `required` becomes false. `PropsWithChildren` never yields `children`. - **Silent misses.** - `export default` with an arrow, `memo`, `forwardRef` or `class`. - Inline `Object.assign` subcomponents, and `Menu.Footer = …`. - In `.d.ts` files: `declare function X(props): JSX.Element`, `MemoExoticComponent`, `NamedExoticComponent` and `ComponentClass`. - Order-dependent renames: `memo(Impl)` declared above `Impl`. - **Precision by rule** on the negative-heavy corpus: | Rule | Precision | | --- | --- | | FC annotation | 5/5 | | forwardRef / class | clean | | function declaration | about 9/13 | | typed arrow | about 6/15 | | HOC wrapper | about 3/9 | | wrapper type argument | about 1/6 | **Structural fix:** a `Detection` contract that carries evidence: - `Component { rule, evidence }` where evidence is one of: returns JSX/`null`/`createElement`, a `ReactNode`/`JSX.Element`/`ComponentType` type, or a known React HOC applied to a component. - `Declined { reason, span }` and `NotCandidate`. On top of that: an export/scope check, renames that never delete an exported base, and excludes matched relative to the source dir. ### B. Silent degradation and miscalibrated guards (P0/P1) - **The empty-props guard drops real components.** Confirmed. On Chakra it dropped 84 wrapper components, and RDT lists all 84. Their props live in uninstalled `@ark-ui`, and the guard only checks the own-prop count. - **Silent rejection.** A rejected wrapper candidate is silent (Codex). Other rules return empty props silently, and only the wrapper rule reports them. - **Cache decode failures are silent.** A truncated payload, a corrupt manifest or random bytes fall back to an empty cache with no diagnostic. - **The opposite problem, noise:** `is_pascal_case` checks only the first character, so `MAX_ITEMS`, schemas and stores each raise `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE`. **Structural fix:** one "declined/degraded" channel with deliberate levels. Reason about guards in terms of evidence of component-ness, not output size. ### C. TypeScript handled as text (P0, six classes) Each was confirmed with no diagnostic: 1. **`Pick`/`Omit` key sets are token-split.** - An alias key set (`Pick`) is ignored, so the props are dropped. This affects the structured alias path too. - `Omit` and `Omit>` are wrong. 2. **`substitute_identifiers` (#69) rewrites inside string literals and qualified names** (Codex). 3. **`extends ComponentPropsWithoutRef` loses Button's props** and reports the element as `"typeof button"`. shadcn uses this shape throughout. 4. **`to_raw_string` drops parentheses.** `("x"|"y")[]` becomes `"x" | "y"[]`, and `(P|Q) & R` becomes `P | (Q & R)`. 5. **The Raw fallback turns unparsed text into `Named`.** Template literals, tuples and indexed access in type arguments all suffer. My `parse_type_text` turns a type named `Infinity` or `NaN` into a number literal. 6. **`extends Required` drops every inherited prop.** There is no step-0.5 arm for it. Adjacent, also P0: a generic alias in prop position, `{ v: Wrap }`, yields `w: T`, and interface default type parameters are ignored. P1 (with a diagnostic): - Object and function type arguments become opaque. - `Omit` loses every prop. - `PropsWithChildren>` is re-stringified. - Display-string visit keys collide and raise a false `CIRCULAR_REFERENCE`. **Structural fix:** item 2.1, structured type arguments (`Vec`) everywhere a type crosses the extractor/resolver boundary. Delete `parse_type_text`, `parse_generic_reference`, `substitute_identifiers` and `parse_string_union_keys`. Add one key-set resolver, used by both the alias and extends paths, and one utility-synthesis path, so that `Required` exists everywhere. Make visit keys structural. Note that 2.1 alone does not fix key sets, `Required`, generic alias substitution in prop position, or the Raw-capture producers (tuple elements and similar). ### D. Incremental state is not derived from the cold path (P0) Each of these happens with a single writer: - **Editing a dependency duplicates the dependent.** Confirmed. A stale `Button` with the old props sits beside `Button (/…/Button.tsx)` with the new ones. Eviction is per changed file, and the key check matches the stale self. - **Dependents are missed.** Confirmed: an edit behind an `export *` barrel and an edit via `../types` both leave the component stale forever. `ReverseDeps` is a second, approximate resolver: it never normalizes `..`, ignores `re_export_map`, tsconfig `paths` and `.js` specifiers. - **Diagnostics are wrong.** Initial diagnostics are never seeded. A dependent's diagnostics are filed under the edited file's key, so fixed errors linger and others duplicate. - **Deleting a file leaves its component and an `IO_ERROR` forever.** The Error-severity `IO_ERROR` pins the exit code at 2. A test asserts the stale entry. - **`update_file` skips cold-path filters:** discovery excludes (an edited `*.stories.tsx` adds `StoryOnly`), `excludePrefixes` and both plugin hooks. - **CLI:** - `watch --out` is not written until the first change. - `r` "re-extract" does not re-extract. - **Vite:** - no removals - display-name keys collide with Rust's disambiguated keys - enums and diagnostics never refresh - the virtual module is never invalidated - `build --watch` stays stale - build failures are swallowed into an empty module, exit 0 - **Concurrency (Codex P0):** state is published piecemeal across five structures, and `extractFileIncremental` runs with no per-session lock. A double save can commit v1 over v2. **Structural fix:** one immutable `Revision { id, global, index, deps, components, diagnostics_by_origin, enums }`. - Built by a single writer under a per-session lock, and published with one `ArcSwap::store`. - Readers do one `load()`. - Cold extract becomes "incremental with every file dirty". Share one assemble-output function, which includes key disambiguation over the whole map, the filters and the plugins. - Dependency edges come from the real resolver. Until then, re-resolve everything and diff; that is cheap at these speeds. - `IncrementalUpdate` carries the revision id, upserts under real keys, and removals. - The Vite plugin pulls the revision and invalidates the virtual module. - Gate: a property test that, for any sequence of edits, creations, renames and deletes, asserts `snapshot() == extract()` for components, enums and diagnostics. ### E. The diagnostics model has no identity (P1) - **82–97% of diagnostics are exact duplicates.** Confirmed: | Corpus | Duplicates | Total | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Mantine | 23,163 | 23,787 | | Ant Design | 4,634 | 5,062 | | react-spectrum | 11,480 | 13,936 | One conditional type is reported 13,358 times. Diagnostics are 9.1 MB of Mantine's 23.5 MB JSON. The same leaf is also double-reported within a component. - **No attribution or position.** Diagnostics carry no component and, apart from skips, no position. - **Misleading help text.** "Enable typescript-go" points at an option that doesn't exist. **Structural fix:** identity `(code, file, span, subject)` with dedup, an `affects: [component keys]` list, and per-run memoization of type resolution, which also cuts time. ### F. The cache trusts a hand-bumped version (P0) - **Stale cache after extractor changes.** Confirmed in code and git history: #69 changed `SourceData` for identical input without a bump. #54 and others did the same. Cached `.d.ts` results stay stale with no signal. - **The version isn't in the payload.** The manifest and the payload are separate renames, so mixed-version tools sharing a directory can decode wrong data. - **The cache barely helps.** It saves about 7 ms out of 150, and `dtsCacheHits` misreports. **Fix:** key on crate version plus an extractor fingerprint, with a versioned header inside the payload. Or question whether the cache earns its keep at all. ### G. Performance at scale (P1/P2) Determinism is clean (six conditions, byte-identical) and so is robustness. Measured costs: | Corpus | Cold ms | Peak RSS MB | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Mantine | 130 | 93 | | react-spectrum | 118 | 72 | | Chakra | 26 | 28 | - **Serialization dominates.** At 10k components it is 382 ms internal, but 2.7 s wall and 1.94 GB with `--json`. Causes: a `serde_json::Value` tree per prop, one big `String`, and two absolute-path clones per prop. - **No memoization across components.** Shared types are re-resolved per consumer. - **Quadratic inheritance merge**, and three `FxHashSet` clones per extends branch. - **Watch saves are O(project).** `GlobalSourceData` clone, `ReverseDeps` rebuild, a fresh oxc `Resolver` with a cold FS cache, and O(A·C) key disambiguation. - **Full HTML mode fails with `--src .`** when `node_modules` is inside the src dir: an off-by-one parent in `resolve_dts`. ESM `./x.js` specifiers are unresolvable. ### H. Evidence, tests and metrics (P1) - **The recall metric** has two flaws: it excludes components without own props, and it matches by overlap of at least half the props. No precision is measured. - **`--format rdt` is not RDT's shape,** and nothing validates it: - a map instead of an array - no `filePath` - quoted default values - disambiguated keys MIGRATING marks it compatible anyway. - **Tests pin the bugs.** - Silent drops are asserted at `extractor/tests.rs:863`, `1128`, `1274` and `1623`. - The watch deletion test asserts the stale entry. - `shapes.rs` "props resolve to nothing" expects a drop, and the Chakra evidence says that is wrong. - Parity tests omit diagnostics and dependency edits. - **Native artifacts never run in CI.** Binding tests, Vite integration and built binaries (`--version`, addon load) are never exercised. Cross-compiled targets ship unexecuted. ### I. Docs and DX (P1/P2) - **Benchmarks.** README numbers aren't in `docs/benchmarks.md`. That doc dates from July, with old tool versions and a removed feature. - **Stale config help.** `config.rs:147` help lists the removed options, and the architecture docs describe deleted invariants. - **CLI.** - Zero components exits 0 for `extract` and `check`. - `check` lacks `extract`'s flags. - A missing `--config` blames node. - A file as `--src` contradicts itself. - ANSI is emitted despite `NO_COLOR`. - Diagnostics lack line:col. - `lsp` advertises hovers it doesn't serve. - **Packaging.** - The license change (AGPL → FSL) is buried in a patch changeset. - No `engines` or `libc` fields. - `STATUS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING` and the fixture count are stale. ### J. Architecture decisions to settle before the backend - **ADR 0007:** separate *component discovery* (structural wins on identity) from *prop completion* (semantic replaces incomplete props). Use separate provenance fields, with `schemaVersion` reserved for the output contract. - **`known.rs`:** hardcodes about 20 library type names (Mantine, Chakra, MUI), which contradicts shapes-not-names and can hide props once dependencies are installed. ## 3. Cross-cutting lessons (process) 1. **Sibling-path parity was claimed, not enforced.** AGENTS.md has the rule, yet watch, the Vite plugin, CLI watch and NAPI each reimplement part of the pipeline. The fix is architectural: one assemble function, with cold defined as incremental over every file. 2. **Heuristics were shipped without negative corpora.** Each new rule (#61, #62) was measured on recall only. Any rule that infers must come with a labeled negative family and a precision number. 3. **Metrics were designed around what we could measure, not what users see.** Precision, exact fields, diagnostics volume, and components without own props were all invisible. 4. **Text stopgaps compound.** Each string parser added to unblock a case added a new silent-failure class. Stop adding them; do 2.1. 5. **Tests codified the current behaviour,** including silent drops and stale entries, instead of the contract. ## 4. Recommended sequence 1. **Hold releases**, the #46 line included, until steps 2–4 land. The stack can merge to `main`, since nothing ships without a release PR. 2. **Precision first (A, B):** - an evidence requirement for the inferred rules - non-destructive renames - an export check - relative excludes - stop unwrapping `Required` - a declined-candidate diagnostic - replace the empty-props guard with an evidence guard Each comes with a negative family in `shapes.rs` and a precision column in the scorecard. 3. **Correctness of the type model (C):** item 2.1 structured arguments, one key-set resolver, utility synthesis that includes `Required`, generic alias substitution in prop position, and deletion of the text parsers. 4. **The watch `Revision` model (D)**, with an assemble function shared with cold, real dependency edges, deltas that carry removals, and fixes to the Vite plugin and the CLI. Gate: the snapshot/extract equivalence property test, plus NAPI and Vite integration in CI. 5. **Diagnostics identity, dedup and memoization (E, G)**, and a fingerprinted cache (F). 6. **A reproducible scorecard (H):** recall, precision, exact fields, diagnostics, time, RSS and watch parity, on five corpora with and without dependencies installed. Validate `--format rdt` against RDT. 7. **Docs/DX cleanup (I)** and the ADR 0007 amendment (J). Then start the backend.

content.text:
Codex's review holds up, and the problems run deeper than it found. Every specific claim I checked reproduced or was confirmed in the code, except its read of #44, where it was right and I had been wrong. The five sweeps found about 60 more defects in the same families.

The ones that matter most, all reproduced on the current tip:

- **Watch and HMR return wrong output even with one update at a time.** That is worse than the concurrency race Codex flagged.
  - Editing a types file leaves two `Button` entries in the output: a stale one with the old props and a duplicate under a disambiguated key.
  - Edits behind an `export *` barrel or reached through `../types` never update the component at all.
  - A deleted file's component and its error stay for the whole session, and so does the error exit code.
  - The Vite plugin never removes components, never refreshes diagnostics or enums, and `vite build --watch` keeps shipping the first extraction.
- **Detection admits things that aren't components.**
  - Typed PascalCase helpers such as `FormatName = (u: User) => string`, `debounce(...)`, `createContext<T>(value)` and zustand stores are all emitted.
  - `memo(Card)` or `getDisplayName(Card)` deletes the exported `Card`.
  - A project whose path contains `.test.` produces zero components and no warning.
- **Props are silently wrong.** These six patterns lose or corrupt props with no diagnostic:
  - `Pick` or `Omit` with an alias key set
  - `extends Required<T>`
  - `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof X>`, which shadcn uses everywhere
  - type arguments with parentheses
  - a generic alias inside a prop type
  - the quoted-key substitution in #69
- **The empty-props guard from #62 dropped 84 Chakra components, and react-docgen-typescript lists all 84 as real.** My recall metric hid this because it only counts components with props declared in the project.
- **82–97% of diagnostics are exact duplicates.** One Mantine conditional type is reported 13,358 times.
- **The parse cache serves stale results after extractor changes,** because invalidation depends on someone remembering to bump a version number. #69 changed extractor output without a bump.
- **At 10,000 components, serialization takes 2.7 s and 1.9 GB of memory,** against 0.38 s for extraction itself.

Several of these are in PRs I wrote: #61, #62, #67 and #69. The underlying causes are a few structural ones:
- Watch, the Vite plugin and CLI watch each reimplement part of the cold pipeline instead of sharing it.
- New detection rules were measured on recall only, never against non-components.
- Type arguments are still passed around as text.
- Tests assert the current behaviour, including the silent drops, rather than the intended contract.

What I recommend:
1. **Hold releases.** The stack can merge to `main`, since nothing ships without a release PR.
2. **Detection precision.** Require evidence that a component renders, stop renames deleting exports, and test against a negative corpus.
3. **Structured type arguments** (roadmap 2.1), deleting the text parsers.
4. **One shared revision model for watch and cold extraction,** gated on watch output matching a fresh extraction after any sequence of edits.
5. **Diagnostic dedup and caching of type resolution,** plus a cache keyed on the build.
6. **One reproducible comparison against react-docgen-typescript** that measures precision as well as recall.
7. **Docs and the ADR 0007 merge rules,** then the TypeScript backend.

The full write-up has each finding with severity, evidence and the structural fix: /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/review/v1-quality-review.md

result: Codex's v1 review checks out, plus about 60 more defects in the same families (watch correctness, detection precision, text-based type handling, diagnostics, cache, test evidence); full review is at /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/review/v1-quality-review.md.

Should I start on step 2 with fix PRs on top of the stack, or would you rather pull #62's wrapper rule out of the default path first?
How long until the sweeps finish? Should we start fixing issues related to the open PRs before we merge them?

The sweeps have all finished. All five reported back, and their findings are in the review I gave you.

Yes, fix before merging, but only for the PRs that introduced defects. The rest can merge now:

- **Merge now: #52–#60.** These are the CI, cache guard, parentheses, enums, unreadable-file, diagnostic-code, builder and detection-rule PRs. None of the confirmed defects comes from them, and most come from code that predates this stack.
- **Fix in place before merging: #61–#70.** Fixes go into each branch, which gets easier once #52–#60 are merged because the stack gets shorter. The defects they introduced:

  | PR | What to fix first |
  | --- | --- |
  | #61 typed arrows | It admits typed helpers like `FormatName = (u: User) => string`. Require evidence that it renders (returns JSX/`null` or has a component return type). Add negative tests. |
  | #62 wrapper calls | Same evidence rule, and reject `createContext`/store/hook shapes. Report rejected candidates with a diagnostic. Replace the empty-props guard, which dropped 84 real Chakra components. Its changeset overclaims. |
  | #64 docs | Its recall figures come from a metric that hid those 84 drops. Restate them. |
  | #66 dead options | `docgen.config.ts` help text still lists the removed options. |
  | #68 shape tests | One expectation pins the wrong behaviour (dropping a wrapper component whose props live in an uninstalled package). Add the negative families. |
  | #69 generics and barrels | Substitution inside quoted strings, a type named `Infinity` becoming a number, and no cache-version bump. |
  | #70 ADR 0007 | Separate component discovery from prop completion, and keep provenance out of `schemaVersion`. |

  #63, #65 and #67 introduce no new defects and can merge as they are.
- **Separate PRs after the stack:** the defects that predate it. These are the watch/Vite revision model, structured type arguments, diagnostic dedup, the cache fingerprint, the scorecard and the docs/DX cleanup.

One caution: release PR #46 picks up every changeset that lands on `main`. Don't merge it until #61 and #62 are fixed; merging #52–#60 meanwhile is fine.

If you merge #52–#60, I'll start on #61 and #62.
Can you just stack them? I won't release until it's clear

Yes. Fixes will go on as new PRs stacked on #70, and nothing changes in the existing PRs. First up is detection precision, which covers the defects #61 and #62 introduced plus the rename path. Reading the rules I'm about to change.

gh pr create --base docs/adr-0007-backend-discovery --head fix/detection-evidence --title "fix: require render evidence before inferring a component (review family A/B)" --body "Stacked on #70. This fixes the detection-precision findings from the v1 review: Codex's P0 on the wrapper rule, the false positives in #61 and #62, the rename that deleted exported components, the silently rejected wrapper candidates, and the empty-props guard that dropped real components.

**The rule:** a new \`extractor/evidence.rs\` decides whether a function renders. It accepts any of:
- JSX or an element factory call (\`createElement\`, \`cloneElement\`, \`jsx\`)
- a top-level hook call (only components and hooks may call hooks)
- a top-level \`return\` of \`null\`, \`children\` or a PascalCase call
- an element return type (\`JSX.Element\`, \`ReactNode\`, \`Promise<…>\` of one)

Generators never count.

**Where it applies:**
- **Typed functions:** arrow and function expressions, functions passed to a call, and function declarations, including \`declare function\` in \`.d.ts\`.
- **Generic wrapper calls:** the first argument must be a function that renders, a component reference, a wrapped component, or a tag name next to an element type or factory payload. \`createContext\` is declined.
- **Renames:** a call alias needs a component-wrapper callee (\`memo\`, \`*forwardRef*\` including \`(forwardRef as T)(X)\`, \`withX\`, \`create*Component*\`, \`observer\`, curried calls). An exported base is never hidden.
- **Declines:** every declined candidate gets a \`SKIPPED_CANDIDATE\` note with the reason. This includes a recorded wrapper whose type arguments name no props.
- **The empty-props guard is removed.** A component whose props live in an uninstalled package is still a component; its \`UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT\` says why.

**Calibrated on the five corpora** against react-docgen-typescript. \`recall(any)\` counts every RDT component with props, closing the blind spot the review found.

| Project | recall(own) before → after | recall(any) before → after | extras before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mantine | 94% → 94% | 87% → 87% | 13 → 13 |
| chakra | 88% → 88% | 68% → 80% | 3 → 3 |
| antd | 98% → 98% | 83% → 83% | 109 → 109 |
| shadcn | 98% → 98% | 99% → 99% | 115 → 112 |
| spectrum | 99% → 99% | 81% → 80% | 229 → 233 |

**Every component lost against the previous build is a correct decline:**
- seven \`createContext\` values; react-docgen-typescript lists two of them
- antd's internal \`PurePanel = genPurePanel(X)\`, which used to *delete* the exported \`Cascader\`, \`Select\`, \`Dropdown\`, \`Mentions\` and \`TimePicker\`; those are back

The first calibration pass also lost real components, and I fixed each one before this PR:
- Mantine's \`tableElement<F>('tr')\` (tag plus payload)
- \`polymorphic<…>(_Box)\` (underscore name)
- React Aria's \`(forwardRef as T)(X)\`
- shadcn's Base UI parts that return \`useRender(...)\` (hook evidence)

Remaining extras (antd 109, spectrum 233) are mostly non-exported internal components. That is review finding A.7, handled in a later PR. Wall time is unchanged: mantine 138→132 ms, spectrum 121→122 ms.

**Tests:**
- new negative families in \`shapes.rs\`: contexts, stores, labels, hooks, helpers, higher-order calls on non-components, non-wrapper calls on components
- new positive families: async server components, rendering without JSX
- unit tests that pin each decline reason exactly, plus \`declare function\`, non-destructive aliases, and components without JSX
- the tests that pinned the old drop now assert the component is kept

Verified: 705 tests pass, clippy and lint clean.

cargo/caliper-docgen-core: minor

---

Type arguments are now carried as structured types instead of display text. Several props that were silently wrong now resolve correctly:

- `Pick<Base, "T">` inside a generic interface keeps the key `"T"`.
- A type named `Infinity` or `NaN` is that type.
- Function-typed arguments resolve instead of becoming opaque.
- `extends Required<T>` keeps `T`'s props and marks them required.
- `extends ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof Button>` yields `Button`'s props instead of HTML attributes for an element called "typeof button".
- Nested object arguments no longer raise a false circular-reference note.

In `caliper-docgen-core`, `ComponentMapping::props_type_args` and `ExtendsRef`'s `type_args` are now `Vec<CollectedType>`. The on-disk parse cache is rebuilt once (schema 11).

`Pick` and `Omit` now understand any key expression TypeScript code commonly uses: string literals and unions of them, a key alias (`type Keys = "a" | "b"`), `keyof Other`, `Exclude<…>` and `Extract<…>`, a mix such as `"a" | More`, and keys passed through a generic parameter. Before, an alias key set picked nothing or omitted nothing, silently. When the keys can't be known statically, a warning says so. The base can also be any type now, including an intersection such as `Omit<A & B, "k">`. In `caliper-docgen-core`, `CollectedTypeAlias::Pick` and `::Omit` carry a structured `keys` type instead of key lists. The on-disk parse cache is rebuilt once (schema 12).

- a key alias, with its own generic arguments substituted
- \`Exclude\` and \`Extract\`

| \`extends Pick<Base, Keys>\` with \`type Keys = \"a\" \\| \"b\"\` | no picked props | \`a\`, \`b\` |

| \`Omit<Base, \"a\" \\| More>\` | only \`a\` omitted | \`a\` and \`c\` omitted |
| \`Omit<Base, Exclude<keyof Base, \"a\">>\` | nothing omitted | \`a\` |
| \`type MyOmit<T, K> = Omit<T, K>\` as \`MyOmit<Base, \"b\">\` | as declared | \`b\` omitted |

def rewrite_fn_bodies(path, names):
    s = path.read_text()
    for name in names:
        start = s.index(f'fn {name}<')
        # signature: decl: &VariableDeclarator<'a>  ->  decl: &Binding<'_, 'a>
        sig_end = s.index('{', s.index(')', start))
        sig = s[start:sig_end]
        assert "decl: &VariableDeclarator<'a>" in sig, (name, sig)
        s = s[:start] + sig.replace("decl: &VariableDeclarator<'a>", "decl: &Binding<'_, 'a>") + s[sig_end:]
        # body: up to the matching closing brace
        body_start = s.index('{', start + len(sig) - 5)
        depth = 0
        i = body_start
        while True:
            c = s[i]
            if c == '{':
                depth += 1
            elif c == '}':
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    break
            i += 1
        body = s[body_start:i]
        body = body.replace('decl.init.as_ref()', 'decl.init')
        body = body.replace('decl.type_annotation.as_ref()', 'decl.annotation')
        body = body.replace('&decl.init', 'decl.init')
        s = s[:body_start] + body + s[i:]
    path.write_text(s)

}

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Pipeline:** Rust core with OXC parsing, SourceData → GlobalSourceData → resolver → ExtractionOutput. Rayon parallel resolution. Parse cache is positional MessagePack; `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` is currently 12 on the #73/#74 branches.
   - **Render evidence** (extractor/evidence.rs). A function counts as rendering if it has any of:
     - JSX, or an element factory call (`createElement`, `cloneElement`, `jsx`, `jsxs`, `jsxDEV`)
     - a top-level hook call (`use[A-Z]`)
     - a top-level return of `null`, `children`, or a call to a PascalCase function
     - an element return type: `Element`, `ReactElement`, `ReactNode`, `ReactPortal`, `JSX`, or `Promise<…>` of one

     Generators never count.
   - **Wrapper evidence** for the first argument of a generic wrapper call: a function that renders, a PascalCase reference (leading `_` or `$` trimmed), a wrapped component (`is_component_wrapper_call`), or a tag string. A tag string needs either an element type argument or a factory payload (`TagNeedsPayload`). `createContext` is declined.
   - **Rename calls are component wrappers only if** the callee is `memo`, `observer`, contains "forwardref" (case-insensitive; the callee is peeled first, so `(forwardRef as T)(X)` counts), is `with[A-Z]…`, contains "Component", or is a curried call. An exported base is never hidden by its alias.
   - **Structured type args:** `Vec<CollectedType>` on `ComponentMapping.props_type_args` and `ExtendsRef` type_args. The text parsers are deleted. `synthesize_utility_alias` handles Omit, Pick, Partial, Required, PropsWithChildren (as `P & {children?: React.ReactNode}`), Readonly and PropsWithRef.
   - **`CollectedTypeAlias::Pick` / `::Omit`** are now `{ base, keys: CollectedType, file_path }`. `resolve_key_set` handles:
     - literals and unions
     - `Never`
     - `KeyOf`, using a detached state
     - `AtFile`
     - `Exclude` and `Extract`
     - aliases, via `apply_generic_args`
     - unfilled in-scope type parameters, which contribute an empty set
     - anything else: `None` plus a warning
   - **`ResolveState::branch()` / `detached()` / `absorb()`.**
   - **Binding:** `Binding<'b,'a>{init, span, annotation}` lets the detection rules apply to both declarators and default exports. `detect_component` runs the rule chain.
   - **Watch revision model (in progress):** an immutable `Revision` published through `ArcSwapOption`, a writer `Mutex`, a shared `assemble()`, and a thread-local dependency recorder (resolver/deps.rs) that records the files each component's resolution read.
   - **Calibration metrics (score.py):**
     - recall(own) and recall(any): recall(any) counts every react-docgen-typescript (RDT) component with props, which fixes the old metric's blind spot.

     - extras

Each `parse_file()` call gets its own OXC allocator. No AST node escapes the function — all extracted data is owned, heap-allocated types. This is what makes the rayon parallelism safe.

The watch path reuses analysis across file changes. A single-file update calls `parse_file()` on the changed file and re-resolves only the affected components.

The current `WatchSession` publishes related state through separate containers: `ArcSwap<GlobalSourceData>`, `ArcSwap<ReverseDeps>`, a mutex-protected named-type index, and `DashMap`s for source data, components, and diagnostics. Individual updates are synchronized, but `snapshot()` can combine values from different moments because there is no aggregate revision identity or single publication point. Create/delete/rename also remains a documented session-rebuild path.

### Target watch publication invariant

Move all query-visible watch state into one immutable `WatchRevision`: global source data, named-type indexes, component cache, diagnostics, and revision/content identity. An update builds the replacement off to the side and publishes one `Arc<WatchRevision>` only after every stage succeeds. A failed update leaves the prior complete revision published.

Gate that target with clean/incremental equivalence. Generated modify, edit-revert, repeated-edit, and session-rebuild create/delete/rename sequences must produce the same canonical components, enums, resolution outcomes, and diagnostics as a fresh extraction over the resulting files. Concurrent tests must prove readers receive an old-complete or new-complete revision, never a mixture. Per-run timing counters are excluded from canonical comparison.

This is AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 ("never fail silently") applied at the config layer: a config the user explicitly wrote getting quietly ignored due to a typo would be a plausible-looking but wrong result forever, and the regression tests for this (`config_schema_rejects_a_typo_d_react_version_instead_of_defaulting`, `try_load_config_surfaces_the_real_syntax_error_not_just_an_exit_status`) are both named after adversarial-review findings where the code used to fail this contract silently.

Stacked on #74. Part 1 of 3 for the watch-mode findings in the v1 review (core). The CLI and Vite/NAPI fixes follow as separate stacked PRs.

## Problem

Watch mode kept its own state in separate containers and re-resolved by a string-built reverse import graph. Verified defects:

- Edits to a dependency reached through a barrel or a `../` import never reached the component.
- New import edges added mid-session were never tracked.
- Deleted files' components stayed until restart.
- Excluded files (stories, tests) added components.
- A disambiguated component's edit could land under another component's key.
- The first run's diagnostics were missing from later snapshots.
- A snapshot could mix state from two updates.

## Change

- **One revision type.** `pipeline/revision.rs` owns the cold build (`Revision::cold`), the incremental step (`Revision::next`) and `assemble()`. `extract()`, `WatchSession::initialize()` and `WatchSession::rebuild()` all use `cold`. Keys, plugin hooks, diagnostics and stats come from one function.
- **Atomic publication.** `WatchSession` holds `ArcSwapOption<Revision>` plus a writer mutex. An update builds the next revision off to the side and stores it once, so readers never block and never see a mixture.
- **Recorded dependencies** (`resolver/deps.rs`). A thread-local recorder scoped to one `resolve_component` call collects three kinds of dependency:
  - **Files read** (interface, alias and template lookups; re-export walks; resolved import targets). These re-resolve on an edit, create or delete of that file.
  - **Bare enum and const-array names**, which are looked up project-wide. These re-resolve when the changed file declared that name before or after the change.
  - **Module resolution.** This re-resolves on creation of a new source file.
- **Changed paths are filtered like discovery** (`discover::is_source_file`). A missing file is a deletion; another read error keeps the previous declarations and records an `IoError`.
- **`IncrementalUpdate`** gains `revision`, `updatedKeys` and `removedKeys`.

## Verification

- **New test** `every_kind_of_change_leaves_the_snapshot_equal_to_a_cold_extract`. After each of 14 steps it asserts that components, enums and diagnostics equal a cold `extract()`. The steps cover:
  - a dependency edit two hops away
  - a barrel edit
  - an own-file edit and a rename
  - a cross-file name collision
  - an excluded story
  - "stops being a component"
  - a syntax error and its fix
  - a dependency delete and restore
  - a const array read by bare name
  - creation of a module an import was missing
  - a file move
- **Mutation checks.** Disabling each recorder fails the sequence test:
  - file recording fails 5 tests, including this one
  - bare-name recording fails the "const array read by bare name" step
  - module-resolution recording fails the "restore it" step
- **Rewritten tests.** Tests that pinned the old behavior now assert the new contract:
  - "deleted components linger" became "deleting a file removes its components and re-resolves dependents"
  - "missing file → `IoError`" in the CLI tests now uses an unreadable (non-UTF-8) file
- **Cold output** compared to #74's build on the five calibration corpora:
  - mantine, antd and shadcn: byte-identical
  - chakra and spectrum: identical components and enums, and the same diagnostic multiset. Resolve diagnostics are now ordered by file, then source position; before, they followed extractor emission order. #5 canonicalizes diagnostic order anyway.
- **Watch repros** (`watch --out`): dependency edit, barrel edit and `../` edit each match the cold extract. All three were stale before.
- **Incremental timing** on Mantine (median of 7):

  | Edited file | Before | After |
  | --- | --- | --- |

Stacked on #75. Part 2 of 3 for the watch-mode findings in the v1 review (CLI).

## Problem

- **`--out` was first written on the first file change.** A consumer started alongside `watch` had nothing to read until an edit happened. This is also why the review's repro scripts raced.
- **`r` called `initialize()`.** After the first call that just returns the current snapshot, so `r` re-extracted nothing.
- **Every TypeScript event rewrote `--out`,** including excluded stories and paths outside the source dirs. That can trigger downstream watchers for no change.
- **Interactive sessions staircased their output.** crossterm's raw mode clears `OPOST`, so a printed `\n` no longer returns to column 0. Confirmed on a pty: output modes were `ONLCR` only.

## Change

- **One `publish` helper.** It tracks the exit code from the whole snapshot and rewrites `--out`. It is used at startup, on each change and on `r`.
- **`r` calls `WatchSession::rebuild()`,** prints the summary and publishes. This covers `tsconfig.json`, `package.json` and `node_modules` changes, which the watcher cannot see.
- **`handle_change` skips events that produced no new revision,** using the new `WatchSession::revision()`. It reports removed keys alongside updated ones.
- **`keep_output_processing` turns `OPOST | ONLCR` back on** after `enable_raw_mode` (unix, via rustix termios). Input stays raw.

## Verification

- Unit tests:
  - `--out` is written by `start_session`
  - `r` picks up a component and an unreadable file that no event reported, and rewrites `--out`
  - an excluded story event writes nothing and leaves the revision at 1
  - a deleted file's component is removed from `--out`
- Process tests:
  - `watch_writes_out_before_any_change` matches `extract`
  - `r_extracts_a_terminal_session_again` runs on a pty
  - `raw_mode_keeps_newline_translation_for_output` failed before the fix (`OutputModes(ONLCR)`) and passes after
- `edit_until_out_is_written` now waits for the startup write, then for the edit. Without that it raced the initial extraction. `commands` passed 3 runs in a row.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean; all 713 workspace tests pass.

AGENTS.md:42:1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
CONTRIBUTING.md:51:**`crates/binding`** — thin NAPI wrapper. Owns the async runtime (tokio) and exposes the five NAPI functions (`extractAll`, `createSession`, `initializeSession`, `extractFileIncremental`, `closeSession`). No business logic.
docs/root-cause-analysis.md:50:**Root cause:** Zero `catch_unwind` anywhere in the repo (confirmed by grep). The three async NAPI entry points (`extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, `initialize_session`) are only panic-safe by _accident_ — they happen to run inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, whose `JoinError` catches the unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not a decision anyone made. Because it was never written down anywhere, every later concurrent/cross-boundary addition reinvented the answer independently and got inconsistent results: `pipeline/mod.rs:260,357`'s rayon `.map()` closures have no per-item boundary at all; `plugin.rs`'s hook loop calls `plugin.on_x(...)` directly with zero isolation between plugins or from the pipeline invoking them; `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`'s `create_session`/`close_session` skip `spawn_blocking` entirely, missing even the accidental protection their siblings get; and `pipeline/watch.rs:93`'s `std::sync::Mutex` can poison permanently, specifically because the unprotected rayon batches and plugin hooks from the first two run while that lock is held.
docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md:9:- `extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, and `initialize_session` happened to run inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, whose `JoinError` catches an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing — not a decision anyone made.
docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md:27:- `extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, and `initialize_session` were already panic-safe via `spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError`; wrapping their bodies in `contain_panic` makes that guarantee documented and consistent with the rest of the codebase rather than incidental. `create_session` and `close_session` were genuinely unprotected before this and are now wrapped directly.
docs/architecture/napi-binding.md:11:- `initialize_session(session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then runs `WatchSession::initialize()` (the first full cold pass). Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
docs/architecture/napi-binding.md:15:`SESSIONS` is `static SESSIONS: LazyLock<DashMap<u32, Arc<WatchSession>>>` — a single process-wide session table. `initialize_session` and `extract_file_incremental` both tolerate a missing session ID by silently constructing a fresh `WatchSession` from the passed `options` and inserting it (`lib.rs:171-179`, `200-208`) — this is a lazy-recovery path, not an error case, so a caller that races `create_session` against `initialize_session` (or never calls `create_session` at all) still gets a working session rather than an "unknown session ID" error.
docs/architecture/napi-binding.md:21:- **The three `spawn_blocking`-wrapped entry points** (`extract_all`, `initialize_session`, `extract_file_incremental`) put `contain_panic` **inside** the `spawn_blocking` closure, not around it. Before ADR 0005, these three were only accidentally panic-safe: `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` happens to catch an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not because anyone decided panic-safety belonged there. Wrapping in `contain_panic` too makes the guarantee a designed one, converts the panic into a `Diagnostic`-derived `napi::Error` message instead of an opaque `JoinError`, and stops being contingent on tokio's internals never changing.
docs/architecture/napi-binding.md:28:`panic_guard::contain_panic` is shared code — the same function backs rayon `.map()` closures in `pipeline/mod.rs`, `DocgenPlugin` hook calls in `plugin.rs`, and all five entry points here. But the failure mode on the other side of an _uncaught_ panic differs by boundary. `crates/cli` is a standalone binary process: an uncaught panic there kills one CLI invocation, and the OS process boundary means nothing else is affected. This crate is a `cdylib` loaded **in-process** into a long-running Node.js server (a Vite dev server, per the doc comments on `create_session`/`initialize_session`/`close_session` referencing `configResolved`/`configureServer`/`buildEnd`). An uncaught Rust panic crossing the FFI boundary here does not fail one call — it is undefined behavior at best and a hard crash of the entire Node process at worst, taking down every other request the dev server was serving. That asymmetry is why `contain_panic` at this boundary is load-bearing in a way it is only "good hygiene" for `crates/cli`: bypass it here and the blast radius is the whole host process, not one invocation.
docs/architecture/napi-binding.md:34:**Invariant 1: no Node caller of any of the five entry points can ever receive anything other than a resolved value or a proper JS `Error` — never an opaque crash, never a native panic message, never a bare Rust `Result` leaking through.** This is what makes `extract_all`/`initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s doubled `Result` handling (`spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` outside, `contain_panic`'s `Result<T, Diagnostic>` inside) necessary rather than redundant — two independent failure channels (task-join failure, application-level panic) both have to be funneled into the one JS-visible error type.
docs/edge-cases.md:140:- **FIXED — real bug, not just a coverage gap.** `buildEnd` unconditionally called `napi.closeSession(sessionId)`. Per Rollup's own plugin hook contract (confirmed against the official docs), `buildEnd` fires once _per rebuild_ in `vite build --watch`, not once when the watch process actually shuts down (`closeWatcher` is the correct hook for that). Closing the session on the first rebuild's `buildEnd` would make every subsequent rebuild's `buildStart` auto-vivify a brand new session (the Rust binding's `initializeSession`/`extractFileIncremental` construct one for any unrecognized/closed session id — confirmed via `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`'s `SESSIONS.get`/insert pattern and its own `close_session_on_an_unrecognized_or_already_closed_id_returns_normally` test) — silently losing all incremental-cache benefit on every rebuild after the first. Not a crash (the auto-vivify makes it safe), but a real performance regression directly undermining the tool's core value proposition specifically in watched builds. **FIXED**: `buildEnd` now no-ops during a detected watch build (`command === 'build' && Boolean(config.build?.watch)`); a new `closeWatcher` hook handles the real once-per-process cleanup. Tests: `does not close the session on buildEnd while watching`, `closes the session via closeWatcher when the watch process shuts down`, `still closes the session for a normal (non-watch) vite build`. `packages/vite-plugin/src/index.ts`
docs/edge-cases.md:142:- **FIXED (coverage gap).** `hotUpdate`'s and `coldExtract`'s malformed-JSON fallback paths (log + send/leave an empty-but-valid result, per their own doc comments) were never exercised. Tests: `sends an empty update and logs when extractFileIncremental returns malformed JSON`, `logs and leaves the virtual module at its placeholder when initializeSession returns malformed JSON`.
docs/edge-cases.md:144:- **FIXED — real bug, found by writing the test.** No sequencing guard existed on `currentOutput.components` mutation in `hotUpdate`. Two overlapping calls for the same file (e.g. a rapid double-save) could have their async NAPI calls resolve out of order, letting an older result silently overwrite a newer one already applied. **FIXED**: a per-file monotonic sequence number, set before the async NAPI call and checked after it resolves — a call that's no longer the latest for its file drops its result instead of applying it. Tests: `drops a stale result when an older hotUpdate call for the same file resolves after a newer one`, `does not let the staleness guard for one file drop a concurrent update for a different file` (confirms the guard is correctly scoped per-file, not global).

- `extract_all(options) -> String` — cold, one-shot extraction. Runs inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
- `create_session(options) -> u32` — allocates a session ID, builds a `WatchSession`, inserts it into `SESSIONS`. Runs **synchronously on the calling (JS) thread** — no `spawn_blocking`.
- `initialize_session(session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then runs `WatchSession::initialize()` (the first full cold pass). Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.

- `close_session(session_id) -> ()` — removes the session from `SESSIONS`. Runs synchronously on the calling thread, like `create_session`.

A Vite plugin that exposes your React components' props on a virtual module and updates it through HMR as you edit.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({

})
```

import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

input.content:
Stacked on #76. Part 3 of 3 for the watch-mode findings in the v1 review (Vite plugin and NAPI).

## Problem

- **The virtual module was never invalidated after its first load.** Edits reached the HMR event but never the module.
- **The plugin kept its own copy of the output, keyed by display name.** As a result:
  - a disambiguated `Button (src/b/Button.tsx)` was written to `Button`
  - removals were never applied
  - enums and diagnostics went stale
- **`vite build --watch` served the first build's output on every rebuild.** `hotUpdate` never fires in a build, and `initializeSession` returns the existing snapshot. Source files no bundle module imports never triggered a rebuild at all.
- **A failed extraction during `vite build` was logged, and the build shipped an empty virtual module.**
- **The integration tier against the real binding has been failing since #71, unnoticed.** CI never ran it. Its fixture `Button` returned a plain object, which has no render evidence.

## Change

- **`load()` serves the session's current output** (`initializeSession` returns the current revision) and awaits a cold extraction still in flight. The plugin no longer keeps its own copy.
- **`hotUpdate`:**
  - sends `{ file, revision, updatedKeys, updatedComponents, removedKeys, diagnostics }`
  - skips changes that produced no new revision
  - invalidates the virtual module and returns `[...opts.modules, virtual]`, so HMR reaches its importers and Fast Refresh still handles the edited file
- **Build watch:**
  - `buildStart` registers each source dir with `this.addWatchFile` and awaits pending changes
  - `watchChange` applies each changed source file to the session
  - the cold extraction runs once per session
- **`this.error` on extraction failure,** in `buildStart` and `load`.
- **CI:**
  - a new `test-integration` job (`just test-integration`) builds the native binding and runs the plugin against it
  - `NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true` makes a missing binary fail instead of skip
  - the job is added to the required `CI` gate

## Verification

- **Unit tests (39), rewritten for the new contract.** They cover:
  - keyed payloads, including a rename
  - invalidating and returning the virtual module
  - no-op revisions sending nothing
  - diagnostics-only changes still reloading
  - out-of-order same-file calls
  - `load` and `buildStart` failing through `this.error`
  - `addWatchFile` per source dir
  - `watchChange` applied before the next rebuild's load
- **Integration on the real binding (5):**
  - the fixtures render again
  - new: a dependency edit and a deletion through `hotUpdate` produce `[{updatedKeys: ['Button']}, {removedKeys: ['Card']}]`, and the virtual module matches
  - new: a production `vite build` bundles the extracted output
- `just lint` is clean, `tsc --noEmit` is clean, and `cargo test -p caliper-docgen-napi` passes 15/15.

## Behavior change

A change that cannot be applied (the NAPI call rejects or returns malformed JSON) now logs and sends no event. Before, an empty update event was sent.

Stacked on #77. Part 1 of #5 (diagnostics identity, memoization, cache fingerprint) from the v1 review: family E.

## Problem

- **82–98% of diagnostics were exact duplicates,** one per component that resolved through the same type. One conditional type in Mantine was reported 13,358 times, and diagnostics were a third of Mantine's JSON.
- **A diagnostic didn't say which components it affected.**
- **Two help texts said "Enable typescript-go",** an option that does not exist.

## Change

- **`Diagnostic.affects`:** the output keys of the components whose resolution reported it, sorted. It is omitted from JSON when empty, as for file- and run-level diagnostics.
- **`Revision::assemble` merges diagnostics by identity** (every field except `affects`) through a `DiagnosticSet`, then sorts by file, line, column and message. Severity uses its explicit rank and the code its name. This respects the documented invariant that neither enum's declaration order is an ordering, so no `Ord` is derived.
- **`IncrementalUpdate.diagnostics`** comes from the assembled output: the changed file's diagnostics plus those affecting a re-resolved component.
- **CLI grouping counts one occurrence per affected component,** so `×N` keeps its meaning.
- **Surfaces updated:**
  - JSON schema (`schema` command and its trycmd snapshot)
  - `index.d.ts`
  - TOON output (`affects:` line)
  - the types and pipeline architecture docs
- **Help texts rewritten** to say what the user can do.

## Verification

Compared to the previous build on the five calibration corpora:

| Corpus | Diagnostics | JSON | Median time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mantine | 24,009 → 563 | 24.0 → 15.6 MB | 191 → 170 ms |
| chakra | 4,538 → 583 | 2.3 → 0.8 MB | 35 → 31 ms |
| antd | 5,313 → 473 | 3.6 → 1.9 MB | 45 → 42 ms |
| shadcn | 3,022 → 2,424 | 3.8 → 3.8 MB | 64 → 65 ms |
| spectrum | 14,231 → 2,575 | 11.0 → 6.5 MB | 143 → 137 ms |

- Components and enums are identical on all five corpora.
- The set of distinct diagnostics is identical, ignoring `affects` and the two rewritten help texts. Nothing is lost.
- New tests:
  - `a_diagnostic_shared_by_many_components_is_reported_once_listing_them` asserts the exact `(code, file, affects)` list
  - the plugin-panic test now expects one diagnostic with `affects: [Button, Card]`
  - CLI `a_deduplicated_diagnostic_counts_once_per_affected_component`
- Snapshots: `affects` is added; Panda's duplicated `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` collapses to one.
- The watch sequence test (snapshot == extract) still passes, now including diagnostic order.
- `just lint` is clean and all 715 workspace tests pass.

## Breaking (Rust API, 0.x minor)

`Diagnostic` has a new public field, so struct literals need `affects` (`Diagnostic::new` is unaffected). In JSON the field is additive.

# 0003. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-07-22 (retroactive)

## Context

The DTS parse cache persists `SourceData` across runs so unchanged `.d.ts` files don't get re-parsed. `rmp_serde::to_vec`/`from_slice` — the default, and what this project uses — encode structs _positionally_: as an array of field values in declaration order, not a map of field names. A `_named` variant encodes as a map instead, at a size and speed cost we haven't needed to pay.

## Decision

Use plain `rmp_serde::to_vec`/`from_slice`, and treat `SourceData`'s field order as part of the wire format. A `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` constant (`crates/core/src/cache.rs`) gets bumped whenever a field is added anywhere but the end of the struct, removed, or reordered — any change that would shift decode position for cache entries written before the change. A version mismatch discards the whole cache rather than risk decoding an old entry into the wrong field.

## Consequences

- Smaller, faster cache files than named encoding — the whole point.
- Adding a field to `SourceData` (or anything it contains) requires remembering to bump `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` if it isn't appended at the very end. Easy to forget — `const_arrays` (added mid-struct) is exactly the case this version bump was added to cover.
- A forgotten bump doesn't fail loudly. It decodes as plausible-looking but wrong data — the worst kind of bug. There's no compiler check for this; it's a discipline problem, not a type-safety one.
